text: Fix the recurrence with the last failure.

Berlekamp–Massey finds the shortest linear recurrence ai = Σj=1..L cj ai−j (mod a prime) that generates a given sequence, in O(n²). Process terms one by one; when the current recurrence predicts ai wrongly by a discrepancy Δ, correct it with a scaled, shifted copy of the recurrence that was current at the last failure.
With 2L terms of a sequence that truly has an order-L recurrence, the result is exact.

Contest use: when an answer sequence is known to satisfy some linear recurrence (DP with fixed transitions, matrix powers, counting walks), compute the first few hundred terms by brute force, run BM, then get the n-th term by matrix power or, faster, polynomial "Kitamasa" reduction (P5487).

Feed enough terms: at least 2L for an order-L recurrence, plus a margin, or BM may return a shorter recurrence that fits only the prefix. Work modulo a prime (the algorithm divides by the old discrepancy).
Product tree; remainders down the tree.

Multipoint evaluation (多项式多点求值): evaluate a degree-n polynomial A at n points in O(n log² n). Build a product tree: leaves (x − xi), each node the product of its children. Then go down: A mod (root product), and at each node reduce the parent's remainder modulo the node's product. At leaf i the remainder is the constant A(xi).

Polynomial division with remainder (O(n log n)): reverse A and B, multiply reversed A by the inverse (NOI 篇第7章) of reversed B modulo xdeg A − deg B + 1 to get the reversed quotient Q; then R = A − Q·B.
Below a small size, plain Horner evaluation is faster, which is the usual practical cut-off (P5050).

Key points to memorise
1. BM: shortest recurrence; on a discrepancy, add a shifted, scaled copy of the last failing recurrence.
2. Needs ≥ 2L terms; works modulo a prime; O(n²).
3. Multipoint: product tree of (x − xᵢ); A mod node product down the tree.
4. Division: reversed quotient = rev(A) · rev(B)⁻¹ mod x^(n−m+1).
